content.title: Asian shares are mostly lower after a wild day on Wall St ends with modest moves
content.summary: Shares slipped Friday in Asia after a day of dramatic swings on Wall Street that included Microsoft’s worst drop in nearly six years.  Oil prices fell more than $1 and the prices of gold and silver weakened.  Tokyo's Nikkei 225 shed 0.5% to 53,119.18 as stocks related to artificial intelligence declined.

content.title: Disco Shares Soar Most Since April on Booming AI Chip Demand
content.summary: Given the Tokyo-based company is known for its conservative outlook, investors largely dismissed its outlook for the current quarter which missed expectations.  “Demand is broadly expanding, including for generative AI and for China,” Jefferies analysts Masahiro Nakanomyo and Hisako Furusumi wrote in a note to investors.  A race by the likes of Meta Platforms Inc. and Amazon.com Inc. to build data centers for artificial intelligence services is spurring chipmakers to ramp up production.

content.title: This Week In AI Chips - Reshoring Boosts Manufacturing Amid Strategic Partnerships and Acquisitions
content.summary: Recent developments in the AI chip industry have underscored the strategic importance of precision manufacturing in supporting critical supply chains. PMGC Holdings Inc. recently completed the acquisition of AGA Precision Systems LLC, a California-based CNC machining company.
